title: Planning a call
description:
Work out the stack space a function needs before a call, under the Microsoft x64 convention.

```
call f(a, b, c, d, e, f) from a function with 24 bytes of locals
args 1-4 in rcx, rdx, r8, r9; args 5-6 at [rsp+20h], [rsp+28h]
shadow space 32 + stack args 16 + locals 24 = 72; 72 + 8 (return address) = 80, a multiple of 16 -> sub rsp, 48h
```
hints: Total = 32 + 8 * max(0, args - 4) + locals; then round up so that total + 8 is a multiple of 16 (lesson 7.06).
Argument 5 lives at `[rsp+20h]` at the moment of the call, just above the shadow space.
requirements: Every call needs 32 bytes of shadow space plus 8 bytes for each argument after the fourth.
At the `call` instruction, `rsp` must be a multiple of 16; on entry it is 8 off because of the return address.
Print the registers and stack offsets of each argument and the `sub rsp` value.
stretch: Check your answer against what the compiler generates for the same function on Compiler Explorer.
